tags.name: Mail
tags.description: Outgoing mail (SMTP) for verification and password-reset emails, and incoming mail (IMAP) that turns emails from users into notes ("mail-in"). Configured through the `smtp`, `imap` and `mail_in` settings namespaces. Mail-in imports a message only when a trusted receiving mail server (`mail_in.trusted_authserv_ids`) reports `dmarc=pass` for the From domain in its Authentication-Results header; with no trusted server configured nothing is imported.

AdminSettingsMailIn.description: Settings namespace `mail_in`: sender authentication for mail-in. The From address selects the account a message is written to, so a message is imported only when the topmost Authentication-Results headers (RFC 8601) carry an authserv-id listed here and report `dmarc=pass` with `header.from` equal to the From domain, and none of them reports another DMARC result. Missing headers, `dmarc=none`/`temperror`/`permerror`/`bestguesspass`, and verdicts from other servers are skipped. While the list is empty and `allow_unauthenticated_senders` is false, the mailbox is not polled at all.

trusted_authserv_ids.description: Authserv-ids (first token of Authentication-Results) of the mail servers that receive mail for the mailbox, e.g. `mx.google.com`; `*.example.net` matches any subdomain. Values are lower-cased, a trailing dot is removed and duplicates are dropped. The server must remove incoming Authentication-Results headers that claim its own authserv-id.

allow_unauthenticated_senders.description: Unsafe: import messages without a trusted `dmarc=pass` (only an explicit topmost `dmarc=fail` is skipped). Anyone who can send to the mailbox can then write notes and files into the account of a user whose address they put in From.
